races.name: Betfred 'Bet Builder' Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent recent form including a win 10 days ago; trainer Gary & Josh Moore in solid nick, Good ground suits (11 wins/places from 15 similar runs), but needs an honest pace at Epsom to deliver late challenge.

runners_data.name: Imperial Cult
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner on a winning streak (two recent victories), though both came on Standard ground — Good going is less proven (2 runs, 1 place), and his best distance of 11-12f fits this trip; class of race is manageable and control of the pace is his key asset.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has placed at 10f on Good ground but lacks wins at the trip; Mark Hoad yard is quiet (0/1 T14), and a field with limited pace means this horse may struggle to find the strong gallop needed to close.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: Strong claims on Good ground with three wins from five similar going runs including a recent win at 10f; Jim Boyle hold-up horse who will look to travel through the race and strike, though 30 days off and Epsom's unique track are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up from 7-8f trips to 10f for the first time in this sample; headgear (hood/tongue-tie) noted, James Owen yard is unusually busy (9/54 T14), and getting to the front of the chasing pack early is his best chance.

runners_data.name: Mrembo
runners_data.note: In-form horse at 12f on Good ground with consistent placing (1W7P from 11 similar runs), but her natural deep-closing style means she's shown in midfield rather than her preferred rear position — pace permitting, she remains a latent threat but the race shape discounts her true chance.

runners_data.name: Beta Reader
runners_data.note: Recent form shows a run of 9th and 7th after placing at 10f; her genuine hold-up style has pushed her into midfield on the map, 55 days off is the longest absence in the field, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 she faces an uphill tactical task.

runners_data.name: Haveagobeau
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win at 10f on Standard and a second in similar company; Jim Boyle runner who will track Imperial Cult and is the most likely of the prominent types to apply pressure late — 32 days since last run is a mild query.

runners_data.name: Turpin
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag attached and zero wins or places from five Good-ground runs; the Jim Boyle yard is represented by three runners here, and Turpin's true hold-up role mapped to midfield because of redistribution compounds the concern — background option only.

races.paceDynamic: Imperial Cult is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to press him from the gun, he can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f trip on Good ground at Epsom. Super Hit and Haveagobeau will push forward from the prominent berths, but neither is likely to seriously contest Imperial Cult for the lead, meaning the pace is controlled rather than contested. The hold-up contingent — Oj Lifestyle, Hello Cotai, and Bobacious — will track from midfield to rear, while Mrembo, Beta Reader, and Turpin are true deep closers redistributed into the midfield map because the field carries more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the back. A steady-to-moderate gallop set by an uncontested front-runner on a track that rewards those who travel well into the straight favours prominent racers who can stay close to the pace and strike early in the home straight, rather than deep closers who need a strong end-to-end gallop to close ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Imperial Cult Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Imperial Cult bowls along in front at his own tempo and the field fails to close the gap entering Epsom's home straight.
scenarios.body: If Imperial Cult bowls along in front at his own tempo and the field fails to close the gap entering Epsom's home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Wears Him Down
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit or Haveagobeau tracks Imperial Cult closely enough to apply pressure in the final quarter-mile and force an error in stamina.
scenarios.body: If Super Hit or Haveagobeau tracks Imperial Cult closely enough to apply pressure in the final quarter-mile and force an error in stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front rank ties up in the final furlong, giving a hold-up horse a clear passage to finish.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front rank ties up in the final furlong, giving a hold-up horse a clear passage to finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If Mrembo, Beta Reader, or Turpin secure a more forward position than their natural style suggests and the race is run to suit a grinding finish.
scenarios.body: If Mrembo, Beta Reader, or Turpin secure a more forward position than their natural style suggests and the race is run to suit a grinding finish.

watchPoints.text: Imperial Cult's front-running draw and uncontested lead gives him a material advantage — watch whether any prominent horse closes to within two lengths entering the Epsom straight, as failure to do so likely means the race is over.

Hello Cotai and Oj Lifestyle are the two most credentialed closers on Good ground at this trip — watch the pace in the first half-mile; if it is genuinely slow, both will find their finishing kick neutralised.

Super Hit steps up markedly in trip (all five recent runs at 7-8f) — watch early to see if Christian Howarth elects to press Imperial Cult or settles, as over-exertion to hold position could leave Super Hit empty late.

Mrembo, Beta Reader, and Turpin are all genuine hold-up types redistributed into the midfield map — watch their starting positions; if any secures a forward berth the race shape could shift, but natural style makes that unlikely.
Jim Boyle saddles three runners (Hello Cotai, Haveagobeau, Turpin) — watch for any stable preference signal in market moves, as the trainer is unlikely to be equally bullish on all three.

races.name: Betfred Play Fred's 5 Million EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Betfred 'Nifty 50' Handicap

runners_data.name: Desert Cop
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course and distance on Good ground most recently (1/6f/GOO) and brings strong similar-going form (15/15 attempts, 1W 4P); held up in rear by De La Sayette, he needs pace to run into and Epsom's downhill finish suits his late surge, though a falsely run race is his enemy.|

runners_data.name: Dream Composer
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up type under Dougie Costello who arrives on a 9-day turnaround for the in-form Tony Carroll yard (11/47 T14); all five recent wins have come at 5f and the step up to 6f is an unresolved question, though he has winning form on Good ground and arrives fresh enough to suggest he is in good order.|

runners_data.name: Amazing Journey
runners_data.note: The lone front runner in this field and the race-shape architect; steps down from 7f having run twice over that trip without threatening, but a return to 6f and a chance to control his own destiny under Saffie Osborne brings him firmly into play — his STYLE_FIT flag reminds that this position suits him here rather than him forcing it, making him the one horse whose natural role the race shape accommodates perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Independent Expert
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up stayer for Denis Hogan, stepping sharply down in trip from recent 7f-8f efforts and returning after 36 days; the redistribution note reflects that the field is stacked with prominent types, though Independent Expert is a true rear-of-the-field runner by nature — the shorter trip and flat-track Epsom 6f ask questions he has not convincingly answered in recent form (1W from 15 on similar going).|

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the Fahey yard under the 5lb-claiming Ethan Tindall, coming back after 18 days with modest Good-ground figures (5/15 sim-going); has placed at 5f on Soft but the 6f Good combination is less proven — sits in a natural tracking position if Amazing Journey leads and is capable of a bold show at an attractive OR of 79.|

runners_data.name: Sir Garfield
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this course and distance on Good ground (1/6f/GOO) which is a strong recent reference point; however, he is a natural prominent racer and the field contains more of his type than the race shape can accommodate, meaning he is likely to find himself pushed wider or further back than ideal — his best chance depends on getting close to his natural position off the break.|

runners_data.name: Goldwork
runners_data.note: Consistent 6f horse for Eve Johnson Houghton with Bishop up, who has placed twice at this trip on Good ground and showed a solid run last time (3/6f/GOO); prominent in style and not overloaded by the field shape — likely to find a clean tracking position at a workable OR of 79 on first-season form that suggests more improvement possible.|

runners_data.name: Mumayaz
runners_data.note: Holds the lowest OR in the field at 72 but has been running exclusively at this trip on Good ground in recent starts (sim-going 5/15) and the Carroll yard have been active (8/40 T14); like Sir Garfield, a natural front-running type who will struggle to secure his preferred position in a field this loaded with pace, and the 7lb claimer Myla Coppins adding her own experience factor makes finding the front even more challenging — his best form needs him close to the lead.|

races.paceDynamic: Amazing Journey is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a controlled, unhurried gallop on Good ground at Epsom's 6f. The pace will be honest rather than scorching, giving Amazing Journey every chance to dictate terms and find a rhythm without burning energy fighting for position. Behind, the field contains more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Sir Garfield, Mumayaz, and Independent Expert are all likely to find themselves shuffled wider or further back than they would prefer, compromising their ability to express their natural style. This shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured tempo — favours horses who can either track economically just off the pace or finish with a sustained run from midfield on a track where Epsom's downhill 6f rewards rhythm and balance; true hold-up closers are structurally disadvantaged by the lack of real pressure to build pace for them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amazing Journey Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Amazing Journey jumps cleanly and is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead without any prominent rival pushing for position early.
scenarios.body: If Amazing Journey jumps cleanly and is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead without any prominent rival pushing for position early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If Amazing Journey sets only a modest pace and the field bunches, creating a falsely run race that sets up a late sprint.
scenarios.body: If Amazing Journey sets only a modest pace and the field bunches, creating a falsely run race that sets up a late sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Force The Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Garfield or Mumayaz pushes forward early and creates a competitive split for the lead, lifting the tempo materially.
scenarios.body: If Sir Garfield or Mumayaz pushes forward early and creates a competitive split for the lead, lifting the tempo materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the race becomes a true test of stamina and consistency over Epsom's 6f descent.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the race becomes a true test of stamina and consistency over Epsom's 6f descent.

watchPoints.text: Amazing Journey's start is crucial — if Saffie Osborne gets a clean break and crosses to the rail unchallenged, the race shape is locked in; watch for Sir Garfield or Mumayaz attempting to press from stalls to force a pace duel that could undermine all three.|

Sir Garfield won over this exact course and distance last time (1/6f/GOO) but is tagged redistributed — watch whether Marco Ghiani pushes him forward early to reclaim his natural prominent role, as this would significantly increase the pace and reshuffle the likely beneficiaries.|

Dream Composer has not raced beyond 5f in all five of his recent runs and his hold-up style at 6f at Epsom is untested in this form cycle — watch whether Dougie Costello rides him any closer than usual given the uncertain late pace.|

Independent Expert arrives on a 36-day break and steps down from 7f-8f trips where he has been struggling; watch his market moves on the day, as a horse dropping sharply in trip who is also a hold-up type in a pace-controlled race needs everything to fall right.|

Goldwork's stall draw and early positioning under Charles Bishop is worth monitoring — as a prominent type in a field that is not overloaded at his level, he may secure a cleaner tracking berth than Sir Garfield or Mumayaz and emerge as the value passage through the race.|

races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Analogical
runners_data.note: Consistent and progressive prominent racer for Sir Mark Prescott, has won twice and placed at 1m4f on Good ground, this trip and conditions look squarely in his favour and Dylan Hogan claims usefully off 143lbs; the key rival to Alma Latina for the position directly behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Mr Freedom
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has run well at this trip and going combination before, Sheena West yard showing 0/3 in the 14-day window but the horse himself carries a solid record at 1m4f on Good; likely to be prominent and gives the race a plausible pace rivalry with Analogical.

runners_data.name: Arcturus Flame
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with three thirds at up to 1m4f on Good ground and wears a hood; naturally wants to race up with the pace but with Alma Latina, Analogical and Mr Freedom ahead of him, Billy Loughnane will have to accept a position further back than ideal, diminishing his chance in the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Sir William
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Charlie Johnston who was placed at 1m2f on Good on most recent start; the step up to 1m4f at Epsom looks worth a query given his best form has come over shorter, and 32 days off means his freshness must be factored positively.

runners_data.name: Double Red
runners_data.note: Two wins on fast ground at a mile but now asked for 1m4f at Epsom; a natural up-with-the-pace horse who will be squeezed out of that position in this field, and Henry Candy's yard is 1/11 in the past fortnight — racing out of his preferred role limits his prospects materially here.

runners_data.name: Central Command
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 82 with three wins from his last four starts including on Good ground at 1m2f; drops to 1m4f-plus for the first time as a three-year-old and wears a visor, the trip is the one open question though his form trajectory is clearly the most compelling in the race.

runners_data.name: Alma Latina
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner for Ralph Beckett, three runs all at 1m on Good ground — this is her first attempt at 1m4f and the stamina query is genuine; if she stays the trip she dictates entirely, but she is tagged with a style-fit flag because uncontested control still does not guarantee she sees it out.

runners_data.name: Timber Twelve
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping up in trip after fair recent efforts; OR 80 and a win over 8f on Standard, with only two runs on Good ground and none beyond 10f — the trip and ground combination is new enough that confidence in his staying power must be measured accordingly.

runners_data.name: Electrical
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping from 8f on Good in his latest run; his best form has been over sprint distances and the jump to 1m4f looks a significant ask for a horse rated 76 who has yet to show he truly gets beyond a mile.

runners_data.name: Tabasko
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old is a natural hold-up type whose most recent five runs are all at 8-10f on ground ranging from Soft to Standard; genuine question marks over the trip extension to 1m4f and he has been mapped out of his natural rear position, making his route to a strong finish dependent on an atypical race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Alma Latina is the confirmed lone front-runner and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the outset, with no genuine challenger looking to push her hard for the lead on this 1m4f trip at Epsom. Analogical and Mr Freedom are the natural prominent types most likely to secure the positions directly behind her, giving the race a settled early shape with a measured pace that is unlikely to become truly searching. This field contains more genuine prominent types than the map can accommodate — Arcturus Flame and Double Red are both natural front-rank horses who will find themselves racing further back than they would like, their style-fit compromised by the numbers ahead of them. A controlled, single-pace gallop over 1m4f on Good ground at Epsom strongly favours horses who can sit handy or just off the pace and produce a sustained finishing effort — prominent-to-midfield types who travel economically and stay well are the primary beneficiaries, while true hold-up horses will need an unusually strong pace injection that this shape is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alma Latina Controls Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Alma Latina dictates from the front at a fair but manageable clip and no rival has the early speed or inclination to seriously challenge her lead.
scenarios.body: If Alma Latina dictates from the front at a fair but manageable clip and no rival has the early speed or inclination to seriously challenge her lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Peg Her Back
scenarios.trigger: If Analogical or Mr Freedom push forward aggressively early and force a contested early gallop that stretches the field before the straight.
scenarios.body: If Analogical or Mr Freedom push forward aggressively early and force a contested early gallop that stretches the field before the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the middle stages and leaves enough of a genuine injection of pace in the straight to allow the rear-of-field runners to pick up ground.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely in the middle stages and leaves enough of a genuine injection of pace in the straight to allow the rear-of-field runners to pick up ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a muddling, moderately run affair with bunching through the turn and multiple horses meeting interference coming into Epsom's straight.
scenarios.body: If the race develops into a muddling, moderately run affair with bunching through the turn and multiple horses meeting interference coming into Epsom's straight.

watchPoints.text: Alma Latina's stamina at 1m4f is unproven in all three of her starts at 1m — if she stops sharply in the Epsom straight having led throughout, the race picture changes dramatically for every prominent-tracking rival behind her.

Arcturus Flame and Double Red are both natural front-rank horses who are likely to be denied their preferred positions by the numbers ahead of them — watch for either being unsettled or making an unexpected move to get closer that disrupts the settled pace early.

Central Command's visor is new headgear and he has only one run on Good ground in his career — if the headgear produces an overexcited early response, his chance of finishing strongly from hold-up will be compromised.

Analogical has won over both 1m2f and 1m4f on Good ground for Sir Mark Prescott and is likely to be the closest market rival to Alma Latina — his ability to track the leader comfortably and respond turning in is the key secondary narrative to monitor throughout the race.

races.name: Betfred 'Follow Us On X' Handicap (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Sarangpur
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good recently (1/12f/GOO) which is the most relevant piece of form in this field, but carries a flagged tendency to fade in the finish — Finley Marsh will need to time the run perfectly to avoid the horse stopping late.|

runners_data.name: Dissident
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with modest recent form (7-6-7-10-7), no wins and limited placed effort on Good ground; Tom Queally takes over but the form line is consistently mid-to-rear and the step back in trip from 16f may suit.|

runners_data.name: Thursday
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form over staying trips but that record is largely on Standard artificial tracks — the shift to Good turf at Epsom over 1m4f is a notable surface/going query for this 6yo who wears a hood.|

runners_data.name: Fram Castle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo with 240 days off the track — the long absence is the dominant concern; naturally a hold-up type who will be shuffled into a midfield berth in a field stacked with similar styles, and the Ollie Sangster trainer strike rate of 0/1 in the last 14 days adds little encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Dotties Star
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Standard at 1/12f/STA and placed twice over 16f on Soft — the form is there over staying trips but she has never been tested on Good turf, and 42 days off the track since that last run means she arrives without a recent confidence-booster.|

runners_data.name: Pablo Prince
runners_data.note: Veteran of 8 years with a solid placed record at 4/10f/GOO and 4/12f/STA, but no win in recent form; a genuine hold-up type who will be further forward than usual yet Karen Jewell's 0/3 in 14 days and the OR=48 mark suggest his ceiling is limited.|

runners_data.name: Stintino Sunset
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — lone confirmed front-runner who will set the pace throughout unchallenged; consistent placed record of 3-3-3-4-3 over this trip on both Good and Standard going is a strong tick, and the headgear combo of hood and blinkers confirms he needs to be ridden prominently to show his best.|

runners_data.name: Head Girl
runners_data.note: Finished 3rd over 12f on Good most recently (3/12f/GOO), which is highly relevant for this race — a 3yo filly who is naturally a hold-up type but will find herself racing in midfield in this congested shape; the Good-ground form boost and David Probert booking are positive angles despite the style compression.|

runners_data.name: Panthere Noir
runners_data.note: Posted a solid 3/12f/GOO last time out in what looks relevant form, and carries a pace headgear (p) suggesting connections want more focus — this 3yo is a true hold-up type who will be compressed into midfield, but the recent Good-ground placed run over this trip is the form tick to take.|

runners_data.name: Lilykoy
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo with just four runs showing; best run was 5/12f/SOF and has not raced over a trip shorter than 6f since, so the 1m4f trip is a query — a natural hold-up type wearing hood-p, trained by Dylan Cunha (2/27 in 14 days) and racing from a low OR=45 base with scope for improvement.|

races.paceDynamic: Stintino Sunset is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 1m4f handicap and will lead from the outset unchallenged, setting a controlled, honest pace on Good ground at Epsom — his recent form string of 3-3-3-4-3 confirms he handles this trip and surface and is not afraid to bowl along. With no rival equipped or likely to dispute the lead, the pace will be steady-to-moderate through the early stages of the Epsom back straight before Stintino Sunset attempts to steal first run turning in, making it a test of finishing quality rather than raw stamina. The entire remainder of the field is hold-up in profile, with Fram Castle, Dotties Star, Pablo Prince, Head Girl, Panthere Noir and Lilykoy all redistributed to midfield positions on the map because the true rear of the field is over-subscribed — several of these horses will race closer than their natural style if the pace allows, and those with the tactical flexibility to sit just off a lone leader and finish will be most favoured. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp, sustained late finish who can time their run behind a single uncontested front-runner — horses that genuinely accelerate on Good ground over 1m4f at Epsom will have a clear edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stintino Sunset Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Stintino Sunset dictates a calm, uncontested gallop and finds enough in the tank to hold on from the front.
scenarios.body: If Stintino Sunset dictates a calm, uncontested gallop and finds enough in the tank to hold on from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Stintino Sunset sets just enough pace to string out the field and one true hold-up horse times a late run to reel him in.
scenarios.body: If Stintino Sunset sets just enough pace to string out the field and one true hold-up horse times a late run to reel him in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Drift Gels
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough that runners from midfield can travel sweetly and deliver a sweeping challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just brisk enough that runners from midfield can travel sweetly and deliver a sweeping challenge in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Stintino Sunset goes too slow and the field bunches, producing a muddling finish with no clear winner profile.
scenarios.body: If Stintino Sunset goes too slow and the field bunches, producing a muddling finish with no clear winner profile.

watchPoints.text: Stintino Sunset has blinkers and a hood fitted — if he gets loose on the lead and sets a genuinely slow pace, the hold-up field will have very little to chase and the straight could become a sprint, completely transforming which horses can win.

At least six horses in this field (Fram Castle, Dotties Star, Pablo Prince, Head Girl, Panthere Noir, Lilykoy) are true hold-up types compressed into midfield — watch for serious traffic congestion entering the straight at Epsom where the course narrows, creating a significant draw on finishing room.
Fram Castle returns from 240 days off for Ollie Sangster — if the horse shows rustiness early or needs the run, it may interfere with others around it in the bunched midfield pack.

Sarangpur is flagged as fading in the finish — if Finley Marsh commits too early from the hold-up position on Good ground, the horse's tendency to stop could cost it the race despite holding the best recent form at the trip and going.

Thursday (Jack Mitchell, hood) has strong form over staying trips but exclusively on artificial Standard tracks — watch for any signs of the horse not handling the Epsom Good turf, especially on the undulating home straight.

races.name: Betfred 'Follow Us On X' Handicap (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Ricardo Phillips
runners_data.note: Well-credentialled hold-up performer under Nicola Currie for Henry Candy — trainer in 0/4 form over 14 days is a mild flag — but the horse has winning form over 12f on Good ground and the 240-day absence needs watching; natural rear-of-field style suits a late-surge scenario well.

runners_data.name: Nymphaea
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact 14f trip on Good ground, which is the most directly relevant piece of form in the race; Marco Ghiani continues the ride, the 6-day turnaround is short but the horse clearly came out of that win well, and the hood (headgear:p) adds a focus angle.

runners_data.name: Just Adair
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over on a horse with an outstanding 7/8 strike-rate on similar Going — two wins and four places from eight Good-ground starts — and the step back from soft conditions looks a solid upgrade; the natural hold-up style means he will need a clear run late but this profile is the most powerful in the field on raw numbers.

runners_data.name: Gearing's Point
runners_data.note: Sheena West runner placed last time out nine days ago, but this 8-year-old is a natural hold-up type who has been redistributed to the lead purely because no confirmed front-runner exists in this field; the 0.80 STYLE_FIT is the lowest in the race and its chance depends entirely on whether it can settle and dictate from an unnatural lead role.

runners_data.name: Arenas Del Tiempo
runners_data.note: Jim & Suzi Best have one winner from eleven in 14 days, and this 8-year-old's last five starts have all been over 13-16f on Stamina or Standard tracks — the step down in trip to Good ground at Epsom is a profile shift; naturally a hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot, its stamina-heavy profile may not translate as effectively here.

runners_data.name: Fighting Poet
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old whose last five runs include a win over 12f on Good but has since posted 4th, 0th and 6th in a sequence that reads as a horse in declining form; blinkers applied (headgear:b), Robert Havlin picks up the ride, and while the style mapping has it in midfield rather than its preferred rear position, the form trajectory is the primary concern.

runners_data.name: High Favour
runners_data.note: Camilla Poulton has no runners in the 14-day trainer window and this 4-year-old carries a clear 'fades in finish' flag — its last four starts show finishes of 9th, 10th, 11th and 10th, and it is the most exposed runner in the field on both form and fitness grounds; Rose Dawes' 5lb claim helps with the weight but cannot overcome the pattern.

runners_data.name: Fletcher
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old stepping up in experience under Sean Bowen for Jim Boyle, whose stable has one winner from fourteen recently; the form string of 00-476 shows a horse finding its feet, and while the 12f Good-ground benchmark (6th last time) is relevant, it has been nudged into midfield from a true hold-up role and has not yet shown the class to exploit a pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Naranka
runners_data.note: George Baker's 3-year-old is lightly raced at this trip but the last run — 2nd over 12f on Good — is the standout piece of form for the lighter-weighted youngsters; Saffie Osborne is a strong booking and the horse is naturally a hold-up type mapped to midfield, so if it can secure a clean passage late it represents a live each-way profile at a competitive mark.

races.paceDynamic: Gearing's Point is the lone confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up style, meaning this race is likely to be run at a steady, controlled tempo with no genuine front-runner pushing the pace from the front. With a sustainable gallop over 1m4f on Good ground at Epsom — a track that can expose those who idle in front — the field will likely bunch through the middle stages and produce a strongly contested finish in the straight. This shape strongly favours true hold-up horses who can produce a late run from off a patient pace, as the lack of genuine pace pressure means closers will not be outrunned early and the race will set up for a well-timed challenge in the final two furlongs.
